$comment: Objects an applied migration file CREATEs that are knowingly absent from the live catalog.
check-ledger-vs-catalog.mjs reports these as ACCEPTED instead of FAIL, and WARNs when an entry no longer matches a missing object so the list cannot rot.

Why these exist: the ledger rows 20260624000050..450 carry no statements. The baseball SQL was applied under other ledger versions with different policy names, so the files and the catalog mostly disagree on names, not on protection. The not-needed entries are where the live protection differs.

Classes: superseded = an equivalent object is live under another name; retired = the table moved to the graveyard schema; not-needed = absent with no live replacement; the reason says what that leaves out.
Add an entry only after checking production read-only. Never add one to silence a real missing object.

entries.name: baseball_stat_uploads_delete
entries.reason: No DELETE policy on baseball_stat_uploads, so client deletes are denied. No code path deletes stat uploads.

entries.name: baseball_log_staff_change
entries.reason: Staff-change audit trigger was never attached; no code reads the rows it would write. Restore with a forward migration if staff audit is wanted.

entries.name: baseball_stat_visual_views_touch
entries.reason: No updated_at trigger on baseball_stat_visual_views; src/app/baseball/actions/stat-visual-views.ts sets updated_at on every write.

entries.name: bpbo_player_read_published
